messages:
Raj Patel: Prom alert just fired for gpu_ecc_burst on gpunode-34 (us-east-1). 12 correctable ECC errs in 30s, then an NVML XID 13 in the kernel logs. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/GPUs
Maria Chen: Can you paste the DCGM and nvml counters? if it's a transient burst i'd prefer a soft approach (no immediate drain).
Raj Patel: dcgm.metrics: ecc_correctable_rate=0.4/s, device_reset_count=1, nvml.xid_last=13. Prom rule showed spike then drop.
Alex Gomez: Slurm jobs on that node don't checkpoint reliably. If we drain blindly we risk big job restarts. soft-cordon first.
Priya Singh: Agree. Suggest 'suspect' lifecycle label so scheduler avoids new allocations but current jobs keep running until threshold. Add a watch window for sustained errors.
Maria Chen: Proposed logic: 1) On ECC spike (>5 errs/min) mark node label gpu.health=suspect and taint: gpu/suspect:NoSchedule 2) Start 10m observation window 3) If device_reset_count increases OR XID errors repeat -> cordon+graceful drain.
Raj Patel: Sounds good. Also add different drain grace periods for Slurm vs k8s pods. e.g. slurm_grace=20m, k8s_grace=5m.
Alex Gomez: We should export nvml.device_reset_count and dcgm.ecc.burst_rate to ensure alerts are correlateable. Also add a noise filter for datacenter maintenance windows.
Priya Singh: Cost note: premature replacement spins up spare nodes and wastes GPUs. Make the automation SLO-aware: only force-evict if predicted SLO risk > 0.7 (based on job criticality tags).
Maria Chen: Implementation hints for drain-controller config (helm values):
```yaml
healthPolicy:
  suspect_threshold: 5            # ecc errs per minute
  suspect_window: 10m
  hard_thresholds:
    xids: 2
    device_resets: 1
  taint: gpu/suspect:NoSchedule
  grace:
    slurm: 20m
    k8s: 5m
  slo_override:
    enable: true
    criticality_map:
      low: 0.2
      medium: 0.5
      high: 0.8
```
Raj Patel: We'll also want a manual override in the console to skip automation per node and an audit log entry.
infra-bot: [alert-log] Created incident INC-2026-204 for gpunode-34 (auto-created by rule gpu_ecc_burst).
Maria Chen: I'll add the dcgm metrics and a new grafana panel for device_reset_count. Tagging @Alex & @Priya for config review. :eyes:
Alex Gomez: Quick edge case — if the node hosts low-latency inference racks, prefer traffic routing fallback to a warm pool rather than draining. Add routing policy to smart-router.
Raj Patel: Action items: 1) I'll open a PR for drain-controller + helm defaults. 2) @Maria add metrics/panel. 3) @Alex update smart-router fallback rules. 4) @Priya validate SLO model for eviction cost. I'll include the YAML above in the PR.
Priya Singh: ack, will run a cost impact simulation after PR.
Raj Patel: thanks everyone. I'll monitor the node for the next 30m and update. :thumbsup:
